references.text: The waters rose over the earth for 150 days, which sets the stage for God now remembering Noah and intervening.
God remembered Abraham and rescued Lot from destruction—the same Hebrew verb (zakhar) is used as in 8:1 regarding God remembering Noah.
God remembered Rachel and heard her prayer—the same expression of God's remembrance and intervention as in 8:1.
God's Spirit/wind (ruach) hovered over the waters at creation, a thematic parallel to the wind (ruach) God sent over the earth to make the waters recede.
The Lord drove back the sea with a strong east wind all night—a parallel to God's use of wind to drive back the waters after the flood.
By faith Noah built the ark to save his household, demonstrating the faith that underlay God's promise to preserve him through the flood.
The contrast between the completion of judgment (7:23) and God's grace in remembering those who were saved (8:1) highlights the transition from wrath to mercy.
8:1 marks the beginning of the waters receding by God's wind, while 8:13 confirms the end of this process and the restoration of the earth.
God's action in making the waters recede (8:1) is confirmed and understood by Noah through the dove's sign (8:11).
